SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Noel Stub is a 74-year-old male presenting with low back pain.
Low back pain began on 08/01/2026.
He describes the pain as achy, localized to the lumbar spine, without radiation. He denies fever, weight loss, or bowel/bladder incontinence.
Exam: Vital signs stable. Inspection shows no deformity. Palpation reveals mild tenderness over the lumbar paraspinals. Range of motion is limited due to discomfort. Neurologic examination demonstrates normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, and sensation.
Assessment: Acute low back pain, likely muscular strain.
Plan: Recommend observation, activity modification, and follow-up in 3 days. Return sooner if symptoms worsen or new neurologic deficits develop.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Patient returns for follow-up of low back pain. Reports no change in pain level since last visit. Denies new trauma, fever, weight loss, or neurologic symptoms.
Minor trauma in a potentially osteoporotic patient.
Exam: Similar to prior visit; mild lumbar tenderness, otherwise normal neuro exam.
Assessment: Persistent low back pain without other red flags.
Plan: Continue observation and activity modification. Re-evaluate in 3 days or sooner if worsening.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Patient continues to experience low back pain since onset on 08/01/2026. Pain remains unchanged despite observation and activity modification. He denies new trauma, fever, weight loss, or neurologic symptoms.
Exam: Stable; mild lumbar tenderness, normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, and sensation.
Assessment: Ongoing low back pain with minor trauma in a potentially osteoporotic patient; no radiculopathy.
Plan: MRI to evaluate for vertebral compression fracture.
